Professional(ish) driver on closed course. Do not attempt. All eight passengers were facing forward at the start and end of every demonstration.

What makes it a Roadster

The other Roadster flies on air. Ours flies on rockets.

A competitor recently showed a two-seat sports car that hops, flips, and hangs upside down using compressed air and fans. Its flying version seats one person and is available by invitation. We looked at that and said: this can be improved. Ours seats eight, flies in every version, and is available to anyone with a deposit.

FULL FLIGHT SYSTEM · 8 × 16 kN

It flies. With everyone.

Eight perimeter rockets line the rocker panels: 128 kN against 63 kN of fully loaded minivan, a thrust-to-weight ratio of 2.0. Sixty seconds of flight per set of motors. Standard on every Roadster, because there is only one Roadster.

BACKFLIP · 1.4 s

A complete backflip, mid-air

Fired differentially, the perimeter rockets rotate the van a full 360 degrees in 1.4 seconds. Every seat, cupholder, and child-seat anchor is rated for it. The rear entertainment screen does not rotate. It remains level. That is premium.

ADHESION ROCKET · 160 kN

Drives up walls. Parks on ceilings.

The competitor uses fans to pull its car onto a surface. A fan pulls. A rocket pushes. A roof-mounted rocket fires away from the wall and presses all four tires into it at 2.5 g, two and a half times what the van weighs. Burn time is 45 seconds. After that, the wall is a wall again.

ORM-100 × 4 · ODDLY AUTONOMOUS™

Rear launch, then landing, handled

Four solid rocket motors in the rear bumper add 400 kN for a 20-second burn: 0–60 mph in 0.43 seconds with eight passengers. At burnout, Oddly Autonomous™ selects the landing site with 100% confidence. Passenger input is not required.

Side by side

Two Roadsters. One family car.

We respect the competition. Their car seats one person in its flying version. Ours seats eight in every version, because there is only one version.

Fine print
  1. “Roadster” is the product name and does not describe the body style, the number of doors, the number of seats, or the vehicle.
  2. Rocket motors are standard on every Oddly Roadster and cannot be removed, disabled, or declined at delivery. Requests to do so are forwarded to the Office of the Chief Executive, where they are read.
  3. 0–60 mph time of 0.43 seconds was calculated with eight passengers, a full propellant load, and 400 kN of thrust. It has not been measured. Measurement is pending.
  4. Flight is limited to 60 seconds per set of perimeter rocket motors. The Oddly Roadster does not have wings, rotors, or a pilot’s license. It has rockets.
  5. Wall and ceiling driving is limited to the 45-second adhesion burn. Plan routes accordingly. After 45 seconds, the wall is no longer considered part of the route.
  6. Loop speed is governed for passenger comfort. If the vehicle does not complete a loop, the perimeter rockets complete the landing. Oddly, Inc. considers the loop completed.
  7. Backflips are performed with all eight passengers facing forward at the beginning and at the end.
  8. Rocket range of 6.3 miles is in addition to electric range and cannot be recovered by charging. Rocket motors are single-use. Replacement takes 6–8 weeks.
  9. After burnout, the landing site is selected by Oddly Autonomous™. Oddly Autonomous™ selects destinations with 100% confidence. The destination remains a surprise to all parties, including the vehicle.
  10. Do not charge during ignition. Do not ignite during charging. Do not ignite in a garage, a drive-through, or a school pickup line.
  11. Warranty is void if the vehicle is operated with its rocket motors, or without them.
  12. Oddly Cars is not affiliated with any other Roadster. Any resemblance is a coincidence of wheels.
  13. Certification: Pending.
